bibliographic.title: A blockchain-enabled IoT framework for smart electro-medical waste management
bibliographic.authors: K. Suresh Kumar, T. Ananth Kumar, Christo Ananth, Mathiyazhagan Narayanan, Hari Mohan Rai, Saurabh Agarwal, Wooguil Pak
bibliographic.citation_apa: Kumar, K. S., Kumar, T. A., Ananth, C., Narayanan, M., Rai, H. M., Agarwal, S., & Pak, W. (2026). A blockchain-enabled IoT framework for smart electro-medical waste management. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-45930-2

methodology.method_family: blockchain-integrated IoT with edge CNN computer vision prototype evaluation
methodology.study_design: prototype-scale experimental testbed with system-level performance metrics
methodology.sample_description: prototype-scale experimental testbed for BIOT-EMW framework; no human participants described
methodology.technology_context: IoT sensing, blockchain auditability, edge convolutional neural network classification for electro-medical waste lifecycle management

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study addresses electro-medical waste management using blockchain, IoT, and edge CNN computer vision; it does not study LLMs, conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, or conversational governance mechanisms.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the article mentions healthcare regulation, traceability, auditability, transparency, accountability, and AI/deep learning in a generic sense, its core contribution is a BIOT-EMW technical framework for waste lifecycle tracking and edge image classification. These governance terms refer to blockchain audit trails and operational compliance in waste management, not governance of conversational LLM systems in regulated settings. High Python triage scores appear driven by keyword overlap rather than substantive alignment with the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic and technology mismatch with review scope is explicit in the provided text; exclusion does not depend on ambiguous interpretation.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects only signals in the provided excerpts. The study reports concrete operational metrics (latency, delay, bandwidth, power, utilization, scalability) for a prototype system, but ethics, human-subject considerations, and detailed limitations are minimally evidenced in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: Within-review relevance is very low because the work is not about conversational or LLM-based systems. Methodological confidence for the review is limited by prototype-scale evaluation and sparse reporting on ethics and generalizability in the provided text.

coding.theme: Blockchain-IoT traceability for regulated healthcare waste operations
coding.subtheme: Edge computer vision automation for electro-medical waste classification
rq_alignment: limited overlap via generic accountability/compliance language only; no conversational governance or LLM control mechanisms

synthesis.main_claim: The BIOT-EMW framework integrates IoT sensing, blockchain-based auditability, and edge CNN classification to enable secure, transparent, and scalable electro-medical waste lifecycle management in healthcare settings.
synthesis.contribution: Provides an integrated technical architecture and prototype-scale performance evidence for automated EMW handling with system metrics such as latency, communication delay, bandwidth, power consumption, resource utilization, and scalability.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text emphasizes system-level operational metrics rather than exhaustive model-level benchmarking; scalability and integration with limited IoT devices are noted as feasible issues in related blockchain waste-management literature.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central evidence on conversational LLM governance. At most, peripheral contextual reference if the review separately covers non-conversational audit/traceability mechanisms in regulated healthcare operations, but not for LLM governance claims.
